_comment: Copy to profiles.json and edit. ONE INSTANCE PER CLIENT (since 2026-09-05): every MCP client (agent) gets its OWN @playwright/mcp server + its OWN Chrome + its OWN throwaway profile directory. Nothing is shared between agents — two agents on the same identity never see each other's tabs (measured: a shared context makes agents overwrite each other's page). http:true => the DAEMON materializes identities and runs one server per client; omit http (or false) => classic stdio child per proxy (v1 profiles only). PIN the version (avoid @latest in prod). ntfyUrl (optional) = your NTFY topic for alerts (or PW_MCP_NTFY_URL env). Nothing hardcoded — only official @playwright/mcp documented flags (--user-data-dir/--isolated/--caps/--proxy-server; --host/--port added by the daemon). PIN a proxy to a profile with the env var PW_MCP_PROFILE=<name> (unknown name = named refusal at boot): N MCP entries pinned on N profiles = N parallel agents.
_comment_caps: The `storage` cap is ALWAYS added by the proxy (identity export/import tools). List extra caps here (vision, pdf, devtools, ...).
_comment_maxBrowsers: OPTIONAL, ABSENT = UNLIMITED (recommended default). Max number of INSTANCES (= browsers) alive at the same time on this machine. A running browser is one an agent is actively holding — the kernel refcount stops it the instant its client lets go, so there are never idle browsers to reclaim. Set it only to cap a small machine (~0.5 GB RAM per instance). When the cap is reached a NEW instance is REFUSED with a named error; a running browser is NEVER evicted. Read once when the daemon starts: changing it takes effect on the next daemon.
_comment_identityStore: IDENTITY = a durable SNAPSHOT of a Chrome user data directory WITHOUT its caches (what Browserbase 'contexts' and Steel 'profiles' persist). Lives in identityStore.dir/<identity>/. Every disk writer declares its ceiling: maxParIdentiteMo (a snapshot above it is REFUSED, the previous one kept), maxTotalMo (oldest-used identities evicted first), retentionJours (an identity unused for that long is evicted). Defaults = Steel's (300 MB / 30 days). ⚠️ Google sessions are DEVICE-BOUND (DBSC, Chrome 146+): an identity born on this machine cannot move to another one — cookies alone die within ~10 min, the directory snapshot survives (measured 2026-09-05).
_comment_instances: INSTANCE = throwaway working directory materialized from the identity snapshot for ONE client, deleted when that client leaves (after the snapshot is saved back if persist:true). Lives under instances.dir. Nothing here survives its client.
_comment_bindHost: OPTIONAL. Address the servers LISTEN on (default localhost). Why you might change it, WINDOWS ONLY: libuv disables SYN retransmission for connects to 127.x/::1 (uv__is_loopback), so a client micro-stall turns a connect() into ETIMEDOUT (measured live 2026-09-05 while two Chrome were starting). The way out is a NON-loopback address that is still unreachable from any network: a link-local address (169.254.x.y) on a virtual adapter connected to nothing, or a private address on such an adapter — in which case you MUST name the adapter in bindHostInterface and the address must really be on it (checked against the OS). Routable addresses (public, Tailscale) are REFUSED: @playwright/mcp has no authentication. macOS/Linux: leave it out, the libuv class does not exist there. Fixed when the daemon starts (like maxBrowsers).

profiles._comment_v2: v2 profile = identity: {identity:'<name>', strategie:'snapshot'|'inplace' (default snapshot), persist:true|false (default true), proxyServer?:'socks5://...' (network exit = an attribute of the IDENTITY, never of the agent), label}. 'snapshot' = copy to a fresh dir, N instances possible, saved back on exit. 'inplace' = the store dir IS the instance, ONE alive at a time (Chrome's own lock), no copy — fallback when a site's sessions do not survive a copy.

work.label: Work account (identity snapshot, saved back on exit)

job.label: Blank persistent identity, one fresh instance per agent, nothing saved back (NOT --isolated: an isolated context is detected as private browsing)

profiles._comment_v1: v1 profile (legacy, still accepted, never combined with identity): userDataDir = a FIXED absolute directory, one browser at a time. isolated:true = in-memory profile — kept as a capability, but DETECTED as private browsing by detectincognitojs 1.9.0 (measured 2026-09-04): not the parallelism mode.
